## Final report — fixed & landed (Gerrit change 2391, MERGED)

**Problem.** `bridge_check_access`'s STEP_CREATE surfaced a raw `FileNotFoundError` (`[Errno 2] No such
file or directory: 'acli'`) instead of a typed transport-unavailable verdict when the `acli` transport
binary is absent.

**Proven root cause.** `run_access_check` (`access_check.py`) wraps the six-step probe in one `try` whose
only handler was a broad `except Exception` catch-all (was lines 237-242). At STEP_CREATE,
`client.create_issue` reaches `subprocess.Popen(["acli", ...])` (`adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:556`);
a missing binary makes `Popen` raise `FileNotFoundError`, which the catch-all stringified verbatim into
`reason=exception, detail="[Errno 2] …"`.

**Proof.** Drove `run_access_check(client_cls=MissingAcliClient)` (and, end-to-end, the real `AcliClient`
with `acli` absent from PATH). Before: `reason=exception` + raw errno. After: `reason=transport_unavailable`,
`detail="bridge transport binary unavailable: acli"`, verdict/rc unchanged (FAIL/1). Mutation check (neutralize
the new branch) returned the held-out test to RED, confirming teeth; run inside `sandbox-exec`.

**Defect origin.** `caused_by = f789-3f9d-8b35-4e0d` (commit `fa1bf138455b`, "Expose bridge operations through
library and MCP", 2026-08-10) — the sole commit that created `access_check.py` and its catch-all (the
exception-leak string exists in no other commit; `--diff-filter=A` confirms the file's birth). Date test:
the leak predates the typed `TransportUnavailableError` contract (`9eb8c34`, 08-15), so it was deficient from
birth (not a regression). Class: **plan_defect** (the originating plan shipped the probe without mapping
infrastructure faults to the typed vocabulary). `--caused-by` recorded on the close.

**Test.** `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_access_check_transport_unavailable.py` — RED-first (asserted
`transport_unavailable`, saw `exception`), held out from the fix subagent, GREEN after, teeth-proven via
seeded-defect mutation.

**Fix.** `access_check.py`: a dedicated `except FileNotFoundError` branch ordered before the broad handler,
mapping a missing/unresolvable transport binary to `reason="transport_unavailable"` with a binary-naming
detail (no raw errno leak). 11 non-test lines; verdict enum, PASS path, and generic-provider-error path
(`reason=exception`) unchanged.

**Scope & safety.** Caller-dependency sweep: CLI / MCP / library facade / standalone script all funnel through
the single `run_access_check` core (all covered); the reconcile-preflight/fsck visibility probe already types
transport-unavailable (`OSError` ⊇ `FileNotFoundError` → `TransportUnavailableError`). Only-incidental callers,
no behavioral dependency broken. Restoration (not new capability), no new dependency, no test weakened.

**Siblings (Step 7).** Axis-2 parity census of the access-check operation: CLI / MCP / library / automated
callers / standalone script / STEP_DELETE cleanup → **no MISSING slots** (single shared core + already-typed
sibling). Axis-1 construct sweep: STEP_DELETE's `reason=exception` cleanup is N/A (the binary cannot vanish
after a successful STEP_CREATE in the same probe). Broader reconcile/mutating transport-spawn paths are a
different operation (parent P1 `54e6-ecb0`, closed) — out of scope here.

**Residual risk.** None observed in scope. (CI emitted advisory module-size annotations on unrelated files
near the 800-LOC cap — `dispatch_one.py`, `applier.py`, `acli.py`, etc. — pre-existing, not touched by this fix.)

**Replication.** Original report no longer reproduces: both the injected and the real-`AcliClient`/absent-PATH
drives now yield the typed `transport_unavailable` verdict. Gerrit 2391: `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`,
0 unresolved → submitted, **MERGED**.
